questions.name: Focus Four: Electrocution
questions.objective: 4.2 Identify controls for overhead and underground power hazards
questions.text: A dump truck bed is raised near overhead power lines. What control is most important?

answers.text: Park closer to lines so the driver can see them better
Use the truck horn as the only warning device
Keep the raised bed and truck clear of energized lines using planned clearances and controlled movement
Ask workers to touch the truck to see if it is energized

questions.name: Focus Four: Electrocution
questions.objective: 4.2 Identify controls for overhead and underground power hazards
questions.text: Which action helps protect workers when mobile equipment must work near power lines?

answers.text: Move the load faster to reduce time near the lines
Let ground workers stand next to the equipment in case it contacts a line
Assume rubber tires guarantee protection for everyone nearby
Use a dedicated observer when needed and maintain communication about clearances

explanations.a: Speed can reduce control and increase contact risk.
explanations.b: Workers near energized equipment can be exposed to step or touch potential.
explanations.c: Tires do not make power line contact safe for workers.
explanations.d: Observers and communication can help maintain safe separation from energized lines. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Focus Four: Electrocution
questions.objective: 4.2 Identify controls for overhead and underground power hazards
questions.text: During electrical hazard planning on a construction site, what should be done before operating a crane near overhead power lines?

answers.text: Identify line locations, maintain required clearance, and use controls such as de-energizing or barriers when needed
Assume the operator can judge distance while lifting
Use a spotter only after contact occurs
Ignore insulated lines because they are always safe to touch

explanations.a: Power line planning helps prevent equipment, loads, or workers from contacting energized lines. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Judging distance alone is unreliable around energized lines.
explanations.c: Controls must be in place before exposure.
explanations.d: Overhead lines should be treated as energized unless verified otherwise by the appropriate utility or authority.

questions.name: Focus Four: Electrocution

questions.text: What is a safe practice before digging where utilities may be present?

Have underground utilities located and marked before excavation begins
Use metal probes aggressively to find energized lines
Start digging carefully until a cable is found

explanations.a: Answer boundary: drawings can be incomplete or outdated and should not replace locating procedures.
explanations.b: Locating utilities before digging helps prevent contact with buried electrical lines and other utilities. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Uncontrolled probing can damage utilities and expose workers.
explanations.d: Careful digging without utility location can still strike buried lines.

questions.text: Which cord should be removed from service?

answers.text: A cord with a missing ground pin, damaged jacket, or exposed wiring
A cord used within its rating and protected from abrasion
A cord inspected and found free of damage

questions.name: Focus Four: Electrocution
questions.objective: 4.3 Recognize safe practices for cords, tools, and temporary power

answers.text: Run cords through sharp doorways without protection
Protect temporary wiring from damage, weather, and contact with workers or equipment
Place connections in standing water if the task is brief
Overload cords because the work will finish quickly

explanations.a: Sharp edges can damage insulation and expose conductors.
explanations.b: Temporary power systems can become hazardous if wiring is exposed, damaged, or poorly protected. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Construction context: water increases electrical shock risk.

questions.name: Focus Four: Electrocution
questions.objective: 4.4 Identify grounding, GFCI, and electrical protection practices
questions.text: During training, a supervisor is reviewing Focus Four electrocution hazards. What is the purpose of a GFCI?

answers.text: To reduce shock risk by interrupting power when current leaks from the intended path
To replace all inspections of cords and tools
To increase the amperage available to tools
To allow damaged tools to remain in service

explanations.a: GFCIs help protect workers from electric shock by detecting ground-fault current. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Inspection and GFCI protection work together.
explanations.c: GFCIs are protective devices, not power boosters.
explanations.d: GFCI protection does not make damaged equipment acceptable.

questions.name: Focus Four: Electrocution
questions.objective: 4.4 Identify grounding, GFCI, and electrical protection practices
questions.text: Which condition shows proper attention to grounding?

answers.text: Ignoring damaged insulation because the tool still runs
Using equipment with intact grounding features or approved double insulation as designed
Removing a ground pin so a plug fits an older receptacle
Using a three-prong adapter without proper grounding

explanations.a: Functional operation does not prove electrical safety.
explanations.b: Electrical protection depends on intact grounding or approved insulation design. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Removing grounding features defeats protection.
explanations.d: An adapter that does not provide grounding can create shock exposure.

questions.name: Focus Four: Electrocution
questions.objective: 4.4 Identify grounding, GFCI, and electrical protection practices
questions.text: What should workers do if a GFCI repeatedly trips?

answers.text: Bypass the GFCI to finish the task
Tape the reset button down
Stop and investigate the cause rather than bypassing the protection
Move the same equipment to another outlet without inspection

explanations.a: Bypassing protective devices can expose workers to shock.
explanations.b: Answer boundary: defeating protective operation is unsafe.
explanations.c: Repeated tripping can indicate a ground fault, damaged equipment, moisture, or overload that needs correction. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: The equipment or conditions should be evaluated before continued use.

questions.name: Focus Four: Electrocution

explanations.c: Cords must be rated and suitable for the work.
explanations.d: Construction electrical safety often relies on GFCI protection or assured grounding methods for temporary power. This is the correct answer.
